text:
sara: Quick check-in — follow-up from the GPU capacity postmortem. I want to lock owners/timelines for the headroom playbook before EOD Fri. Main items: quota guardrails, scheduler tuning, emergency headroom policy, and automated reminders.

miguel: +1. I can take quota guardrails (evaluate committed vs burst capacity + throttle policy). Target: proposal by Tue.

kevin: I'll own scheduler tuning (priority classes + bin-packing tweaks). Plan to run a small perf sweep Wed/Thu and share numbers.

ashley: I'll draft the emergency headroom policy + runbooks (what to do at 10%, 5%, <3% spare GPUs). Will need input from kevin for thresholds.

dmitri: For automation I can wire up an ops-bot job to post alerts and create Jira tickets when headroom crosses thresholds. Ops-bot can also run the weekly capacity snapshot.

jane: Adding product perspective: can we add a soft-fallback model routing policy (route to smaller quantized variants) as part of this playbook? That reduces immediate pressure. I'll draft requirements.

miguel: For quota guardrails — thinking: enforce per-customer burst caps + a global emergency throttle that can be toggled by SRE. Also add a quota "credit" system for short spikes.

kevin: Agreed. Scheduler tuning notes I'm planning to test: 1) increase bin-packing scoring weight for memory to reduce fragmentation; 2) tune kube-scheduler affinity for long-running model pods; 3) try group preemption only for preemptible pools.

ashley: I sketched runbook sections: detection, comms, mitigation, rollback. Example mitigation step: "flip to reduced-core quantized model pool for 2 min, evaluate latency impact". Need exact commands.

kevin: Here's a quick config snippet I want to try in staging (pseudo-yaml):

```
policy:
  binPacking:
    weightMemory: 1.5
    weightCPU: 1.0
  preemption:
    enabled: true
    scope: group
  headroomThreshold: 0.20  # keep 20% spare GPUs
```

sara: Nice. Couple of constraints: Managed Dedicated customers need separate policies (cannot auto-migrate). Add a note for dedicated vs hosted.

dmitri: ops-bot will post daily snapshot to #eng-sre and create a ticket if spare_gpus < 15% for two consecutive checks. I can prototype the alert rule:

```
alert: LowSpareGPUs
expr: spare_gpus_percent < 15
for: 10m
labels: { severity: "warning" }
```

miguel: Timeline roundup: I can deliver quota guardrails proposal by Tue EOD (1955640000). Kevin will post tuning results by Thu (1955812800). Ashley will draft runbook by Fri (1955899200). Dmitri to prototype ops-bot alert by next Mon (1956032000). Jane to send fallback routing requirements by Tue (1955640000).

sara: Assigning owners in thread — I'll create a follow-up doc and link back here. Ops: add a weekly recurring checkpoint for these items until closed. @ops-bot can you set a recurring reminder?

ops-bot: created-reminder: "Headroom playbook weekly sync" every Monday 09:30 in #incidents. First run: 1955614200. (reacts: :white_check_mark:)

kevin: Quick question — do we want a safety cap on new model rollouts when spare_gpus < 25%? Might prevent regressions during ramps.

jane: From product side, yes — soft cap sounds good. We can disable auto-rollout and require manual approval past threshold.

ashley: I'll add that to the runbook: "auto-rollouts disabled when spare_gpus < 25% — manual approval required."

miguel: One more ask: can we add a short post-incident eval checklist to ensure root cause changes had the intended effect? e.g., run a spike test 48h after rollout.

sara: Good call. We'll build a 48h validation into the playbook and tie it to the Jira remediation ticket.

dmitri: I'll add a hook so that when the remediation ticket is closed, ops-bot schedules a spike test job and posts results in thread.

sara: OK — owners & checkpoints consolidated:
- quota guardrails: miguel (proposal Tue 1955640000)
- scheduler tuning tests: kevin (results Thu 1955812800)
- emergency headroom runbook + rollout caps: ashley (draft Fri 1955899200)
- ops-bot alerts + snapshot job: dmitri (prototype Mon 1956032000)
- fallback routing reqs: jane (Tue 1955640000)

sara: If no objections I'll open the Jira tickets now and tag owners. We can close this thread when all tickets are created and initial proposals posted.

kevin: No objections.

miguel: go ahead.

jane: thanks — will coordinate on the fallback model list.

ops-bot: jira-ticket-created: REM-7123 assigned-to: miguel, REM-7124 assigned-to: kevin, REM-7125 assigned-to: ashley (links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/REM-7123).

sara: Perfect. Thanks everyone. I'll push the doc and tagging now. We'll review during the weekly ops check-in. :thumbsup:
